spec_match.rationale: The contract rows are lifted from spec §3.1.6 verbatim (roles, tab stops, activation focus, focus scope, tree pruning) and from the propdef's computed-value line, with the explainer's reference AX trees linked.

interactive.rationale: Two live carousels apply the two declared modes for real, a run button re-executes the parse and computed-value probes, and both per-carousel notes plus two measured table cells update from the browser's answers.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises measured-where-measurable and manual-observation labels where not; the table does exactly that split.

edge_cases.rationale: Probes all four keyword forms independently (catching this build's position-first-only parsing), and the fallback path when a declaration is rejected is applied and reported per carousel.

references.rationale: Chromestatus entry, scroll-marker-modes spec section, and the explainer gist with reference accessibility trees.

conformance.rationale: Mirrors the feature suite exactly: scriptable contracts asserted, the role/keyboard contract recorded as manual with its reason.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP run on Chromium 141: run button produced 'after links true / after tabs true / links false / tabs false', the computed-normalization cell reported plain after computing to 'after links', both carousels applied their declarations, zero console errors; desktop and 360px screenshots read. Out-of-band CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree confirmed the manual rows are genuinely unmeasurable from page JS.

telemetry_health.rationale: inspector-probes-ran asserts on every run plus a paired inspector-modes-parse / inspector-modes-rejected-fallback assert covering both branches.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout; measured cells use emerald/rose on paper; the manual-observation tag is stone/charcoal with a black border; run button sets background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: Real table semantics with caption and row/column headers, aria-live status output, labelled carousels, focus-visible on button and markers; the manual rows give screen-reader-relevant instructions rather than unverifiable claims.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Carousel pair stacks to one column under 640px; the wide contract table sits in its own overflow-x scroller so documentElement.scrollWidth stays 360 under mobile emulation; markers and button meet tap-target size.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible tabs keyboard interaction roving tabindex
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Verify semantics with the browser's accessibility-tree inspector rather than assuming attribute presence or absence tells the story.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The page's whole design routes role/focus/pruning contracts to DevTools AX inspection with per-row instructions, because pseudo-element AX state is not scriptable; nothing unmeasurable is scored by the page.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive comparison table without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Only tables/diagrams may exceed the page width, each inside its own overflow-x auto container; grids collapse to one column when narrow.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The 4-column contract table has min-width 640px inside a .scroller with overflow-x auto; the carousel pair is a grid that stacks below 640px.

openQuestions.title: Fill the measured column with real Chrome 154 AX evidence
openQuestions.detail: The manual rows currently instruct the visitor. Once the verification environment has a Chrome 154 binary, capture the AX tree for both carousels (links: navigation/link roles; tabs: tablist/tab/tabpanel + pruning) and cite the observed divergence in the page copy — on the Chromium 141 build browser both modes still expose tablist/tab and no pruning, which is exactly why the page refuses to claim otherwise.

summary: Contract-by-contract comparison of links vs tabs mode with a strict measured/manual split: parse and computed-value contracts probed live per keyword, accessibility contracts routed to DevTools with instructions, and honest handling of this build's position-first-only parsing.
